agent.problem: Solomon appears for the first time, but he is only named as the owner of the collection. The opening never briefly says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

agent.problem: This blanks out the final word of a line the baker has not seen. Card 6 only describes testing silver and gold, so it does not give the baker enough context to reason that the LORD tests hearts rather than kings or nations.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

agent.problem: "That bear" points back to the bear introduced on story card 4, which is no longer on screen. The question should stand alone, for example by saying "a bear robbed of her cubs."

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Card 13 says only that the fool is not buying something. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker distinguish wisdom from land or cattle, so this is an uninformed guess at the unseen wording of the line.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

agent.problem: Loving "when things go well" and "when love is returned" are both included in loving "at all times." A baker could defend either alternative, so neither is a reliably false answer.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
